# How to Analyze User Testing Results in TheySaid: A Step-by-Step Guide

Chris Hicken - Co-founder at TheySaid

by

Chris

–

Last Update:

October 26, 2026

Running a user test is the easy part. The hard part is turning hours of recordings and hundreds of answers into a clear list of what's working, what's broken, and what to fix first.

TheySaid does that work for you. Every session is recorded, transcribed, and lined up against your questions, and AI analysis turns all of it into evidence-backed findings and ranked recommendations. This guide walks through the full process with screenshots, using a real example: a test of how people shop for a home office monitor on Lenovo.com, run with five AI testers. [...] You can also write your own skill with the help of the AI Companion. Just describe what you want, and it drafts the skill for you. In this example, it built a Usability Findings Analyzer that sorts findings into Working, Broken, and Missing and ranks recommendations by impact. For the full walkthrough, see Part 4 of How to Set Up a User Test in TheySaid.

## Step 5: Run the analysis and read the verdict

Your analysis opens as its own tab in the Analysis view. It takes a minute or two to generate. If you change your skill or get new responses, click the analysis name and choose Re-run. Keep in mind that re-running replaces the current version, and the old one can't be recovered.

## Start testing in minutes

That’s the whole setup: describe your test, let AI write it, polish it in the Builder, and publish. In under two minutes, you’ll have a live, AI-moderated test running with real users, synthetic audiences, or both.

And this is only the start of what’s new in TheySaid 4.0. Write your own Skills with the AI Companion, launch tests right where you build in tools like Claude Design, and turn every session into clear, evidence-backed next steps, plus so much more.

Ready to see how users will react? Get started for free and run your first test today.

Read How to Analyze User Testing Results in TheySaid to turn every session into clear findings and next steps.

## FAQs [...] Can I use my own voice for the AI moderator? Yes. Go to Moderator Voice, record a short sample of yourself reading one sentence, pick a mood (Neutral, Warm, Professional, or Energetic), and save it. TheySaid builds the voice in under a minute, and you can make it the default for all your tests.

Can I launch a TheySaid test from my design tool? Yes. With TheySaid 4.0, you can plan and launch a test right where you build. In Claude Design, for example, you can ask Claude to write a test plan for your prototype and launch it in TheySaid without leaving your design.

| [...] The Builder has two main areas:

 The preview (center) shows exactly what participants will see. Use the Preview / Logic toggle at the top to switch between how the test looks and how questions branch.
 The Build panel (right) lists every item in order, labeled by type. Click any item to edit it, or drag it to reorder.

At the top of the Build panel, you'll find a Screener block. Turn it on to ask a few qualifying questions before the test starts, so only the right people take part. At the bottom, the Outro holds your closing message, like Thank you for taking this test!
